property_summary: After the admin calls setOwner with any argument, the owner must equal the supplied _owner input according to the original contract; the buggy version instead sets owner to msg.sender, so for any admin other than the supplied _owner the equality fails.
After a non-admin calls setOwner, the call must revert according to the original contract; the buggy version still sets owner to the caller's address, breaking the onlyAdmin restriction.

After any call to setOwner, owner must equal the newly set owner value returned by a subsequent call to a public getter; the buggy version violates this by setting owner to msg.sender regardless of the _owner parameter.

After any call to setOwner through the onlyAdmin modifier, the owner stored in the contract must equal the _owner argument passed; the mutant breaks this because it ignores the argument and keeps the old owner.

For any sender that is the admin, after calling setOwner(_owner), the public variable owner must equal _owner; the buggy mutant ignores _owner and leaves owner unchanged, so owner differs from _owner after the call.

The invariant is that for any sender who is the admin, calling setOwner with any address argument will result in the contract's owner state variable being updated to that argument; the bug violates this by ignoring the argument and leaving owner unchanged.
After any call to setOwner with a non-zero address, the owner variable must equal the passed argument; the mutant always sets owner to address(0), violating this rule.

After a successful call to setOwner with a non-admin caller, owner must not change; the mutant incorrectly sets owner to address(0) even when call reverts, but the rule targets successful calls by admin.
Only the admin can change the owner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner.
The owner can only be changed by the admin; the bug allows any non-admin caller to change the owner, violating strict admin-only access control.
The owner set by any non-admin caller must be the same as the owner set by the admin's call with the same argument; the bug allows a non-admin to set a different owner, violating this consistency.

After any call to setOwner(_newOwner) from any caller, the owner variable becomes the _newOwner argument; the reference always enforces admin-only access so the property holds only for the admin, while the bug allows non-admin callers to change owner to _newOwner, making the property false for those callers.

For any caller, setOwner can only succeed when called by the original admin (reference), whereas the mutant allows any non-zero-address caller to succeed because the check requires msg.sender == address(0), which is impossible for an EOA, effectively making the onlyAdmin modifier always revert.

For any caller that is not the deployer, the reference contract's setOwner call always reverts, while the mutant's setOwner call always reverts (since no caller can be the zero address), making them indistinguishable; however, when the deployer calls setOwner, the reference succeeds and the mutant reverts, so the property 'call succeeds iff caller is deployer' distinguishes them.

For any caller, a non-admin call to setOwner must not change the owner; the mutant allows anyone to change the owner because the zero-address check always fails, making the modifier revert and thus setOwner never executes and never changes the owner — but both always revert for non-admins, so the real difference is that even the admin can no longer change the owner, which is captured by asserting that after any call, owner remains the original deployer address.
For any caller, a successful call to setOwner must set owner to the provided address; the buggy version makes every call revert, so owner never changes.
For any caller, a call to setOwner that does not revert must set the owner to the supplied address; the buggy version reverts for every caller including the admin, so the owner can never be changed.
